ko: 의식이 끝난 밤 젊은 신도 하나가 향유 병을 들고 당신의 방문 앞에 서 있습니다. 얇은 옷자락 사이로 촛불이 비칩니다.
mt: On the night of the ceremony, a young gentleman is standing before your door with a oil bottle, with a candle shining through the thin skirt.
en: The night after the ritual, a young follower stands at your door holding a bottle of scented oil. Candlelight shows through the thin folds of their robe.

ko: 신도들이 목욕재계 의식을 함께 치르자고 청합니다. 김이 서린 대욕장 물 위에 장미 꽃잎이 떠 있습니다.
mt: The faithful ask us to join them in their bath-making ritual, and there's rose petals on Kim's baths.
en: Your followers ask you to join them in a ritual bath of purification. Rose petals float on the steaming water of the great bathhouse.

ko: 부유한 미망인이 거액의 봉헌금을 내밀며 단둘이 기도하고 싶다고 청합니다. 그녀의 목에서 진주가 빛납니다.
mt: A wealthy widow holds out a large dedication fund and asks to be prayed alone, and pearls shine from her neck.
en: A wealthy widow holds out a lavish offering and asks to pray with you alone. Pearls gleam at her throat.

ko: 당신의 손길이 병을 낫게 한다는 소문이 돕니다. 대기실에 맨어깨를 드러낸 신도들이 줄지어 앉아 있습니다.
mt: There's a rumor that your hand heals the disease, and there's a line of believers in the waiting room with their bare shoulders on their backs.
en: Word spreads that your touch heals the sick. Followers sit in rows in the waiting room, their shoulders bare.

ko: 보름달 아래 춤의 의식을 열자는 제안이 올라옵니다. 마당에는 북과 횃불이 준비되어 있습니다.
mt: There's a proposal to open the ritual of dancing under the full moon, and there's drums and torches in the yard.
en: Someone proposes a dance ritual beneath the full moon. Drums and torches stand ready in the courtyard.

ko: 간택을 원하는 신도들이 하얀 비단만 걸친 채 제단 앞에 늘어섰습니다. 그들의 시선이 모두 당신에게 꽂혀 있습니다.
mt: A group of believers who wanted to make a choice spread out in front of the altar with only white silk, and their eyes are all on you.
en: Followers hoping to be chosen line up before the altar, wrapped in nothing but white silk. Every eye is fixed on you.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 오래 잠들어 있던 열기를 기억해 냅니다. 손끝이 저리고 숨이 가빠집니다.
mt: The host's body remembers the long-sleep heat, and the fingertips are gone, and his breath is gone.
en: The host's body remembers a heat that has slept in it for years. Your fingertips tingle and your breath quickens.

ko: 한 화가가 신의 나신을 그리고 싶다며 찾아왔습니다. 그의 화첩에는 이미 당신의 얼굴이 가득합니다.
mt: A painter came to me, wanting to draw for God's health, and his collection is already full of your face.
en: A painter comes asking to paint the god in the nude. His sketchbook is already full of your face.

ko: 신도 부부가 당신의 축복 아래 첫날밤을 보내고 싶다고 청합니다. 신방에는 붉은 초가 켜져 있습니다.
mt: The Shinto couple are asking to spend their first night under your blessing.
en: A married couple of followers ask to spend their wedding night under your blessing. Red candles burn in the bridal chamber.

ko: 향을 피운 밀실에서 황홀경 기도회를 열자는 의견이 나옵니다. 향로에서 달콤하고 무거운 연기가 피어오릅니다.
mt: The idea is to open a crescendo in a scented wheat room, where sweet, heavy smoke blooms from the furnace.
en: Someone suggests holding an ecstatic prayer meeting in an incense-filled back room. Sweet, heavy smoke curls from the censer.

ko: 당신을 흠모하는 신도들이 연서를 산더미처럼 보내왔습니다. 봉투마다 향수 냄새가 짙게 배어 있습니다.
mt: The faithful who took care of you have sent you around like a pile of paper, and every envelope has a very high scent of perfume.
en: Adoring followers have sent you a mountain of love letters. Every envelope reeks of perfume.

ko: 무희 출신 신도가 신전에서 바치는 춤을 추겠다고 합니다. 그녀의 발목에서 작은 방울이 울립니다.
mt: The Muhee Shintoist says he's going to dance at the temple, and a little droplet goes off her ankle.
en: A follower who was once a dancer offers to perform a sacred dance in the temple. Tiny bells chime at her ankles.

ko: 당신의 꿈에 신도들이 하나둘 찾아왔다는 증언이 쏟아집니다. 그들은 모두 같은 꿈을 꾸었다고 말합니다.
mt: There's evidence that the faithful have come to one or two in your dreams, and they all say you've had the same dream.
en: Testimonies pour in that followers have been visiting you in your dreams, one after another. They all say they dreamed the same dream.

ko: 새로 들어온 신도가 당신의 발에 입을 맞추게 해 달라고 애원합니다. 그는 무릎을 꿇은 채 떨고 있습니다.
mt: A new Shintoist begs you to kiss your feet. He's on his knees trembling.
en: A new follower begs to be allowed to kiss your feet. He trembles on his knees.

ko: 한밤의 온천 순례를 떠나자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 산중 노천탕에서 김이 피어오릅니다.
mt: It's suggested that we leave the annual hot spring pilgrimage, and Kim is coming up from the middle of the mountain in the open water.
en: Someone proposes a midnight pilgrimage to the hot springs. Steam rises from an open-air bath deep in the mountains.

ko: 신도들이 모은 봉헌금으로 황금 욕조를 들이자는 의견이 나옵니다. 견적서에 적힌 숫자가 눈부십니다.
mt: It's an opinion for the faithful to take the golden bath with a collection of bags, and the number on the checkbook is brilliant.
en: Someone suggests spending the followers' offerings on a golden bathtub. The figure on the quote is dazzling.

ko: 보석상이 신에게 어울릴 왕관을 가져왔습니다. 벨벳 상자 안에서 루비가 핏빛으로 빛납니다.
mt: The jeweler has brought a crown to suit the gods, and in the velvet box, the ruby shines blood.
en: A jeweler brings a crown fit for a god. In its velvet box, a ruby glows the color of blood.

ko: 부유한 사업가가 교단에 고급 별장을 바치겠다고 합니다. 바다가 내려다보이는 통유리 저택입니다.
mt: A wealthy businessman says he's going to give a fancy star sign to a school, a glass house that looks like the ocean.
en: A wealthy businessman offers to give the cult a luxury villa. It is a glass-walled mansion overlooking the sea.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 옷을 금실로 다시 지어 바치겠다고 합니다. 재단사가 줄자를 들고 기다립니다.
mt: They say they're going to put your clothes back on and give them to you, and the tailor is waiting for you with a tape measure.
en: Your followers offer to remake your robes in gold thread. A tailor waits with a measuring tape.

ko: 봉헌금이 금고에 넘쳐납니다. 지폐 다발이 바닥까지 쌓여 금고 문이 닫히지 않습니다.
mt: The deposition is in the vault. The vault doors are not closed, the bills are piled up to the floor.
en: Offerings overflow the vault. Bundles of bills are stacked to the floor, and the vault door will not close.

ko: 수입 명차를 신의 수레로 삼자는 제안이 들어왔습니다. 전시장의 검은 차체가 거울처럼 반짝입니다.
mt: It's suggested that we take the revenue car as God's wagon, and the black car at the exhibition is as shiny as a mirror.
en: Someone proposes making an imported luxury car the god's chariot. Its black body gleams like a mirror in the showroom.

ko: 신도 하나가 집안의 가보를 바치겠다고 들고 왔습니다. 오래된 비취 함에서 서늘한 빛이 납니다.
mt: A member of the congregation has come to offer the family heirloom, and it's a cool light from an old jade.
en: A follower brings a family heirloom as an offering. A cold light glows from an old jade box.

ko: 신전 기둥에 금박을 입히자는 의견이 나옵니다. 장인이 금박 견본을 햇빛에 비추어 보입니다.
mt: The idea is to put a gold gourd on the temple column, and the man shows the gold samples in the sunlight.
en: Someone suggests gilding the temple pillars. A craftsman holds a sample of gold leaf up to the sunlight.

ko: 복권에 당첨된 신도가 당첨금의 절반을 바치겠다고 합니다. 그는 당신이 번호를 점지해 주었다고 믿습니다.
mt: The Shintoist who won the lottery says he's willing to give half of his winnings, and he believes you've got the number.
en: A follower who won the lottery offers half his winnings. He believes you chose the numbers for him.

ko: 경매장에 신화 시대의 성배가 나왔다는 소식이 들어옵니다. 시작가부터 숨이 막힙니다.
mt: There's news in the auction that there's an infratern of the ShinHwa era, which chokes at the beginning.
en: Word comes that a holy grail from the age of myth has turned up at auction. Even the opening bid takes your breath away.

ko: 명품 매장이 신의 이름을 붙인 한정판을 내자고 제안합니다. 시안 속 가방에 당신의 문장이 금빛으로 박혀 있습니다.
mt: I suggest that you give a limited edition with the name of God on it, and your sentence is gold in the bag inside the city.
en: A luxury brand proposes a limited edition bearing the god's name. In the mockup, your emblem is stamped in gold on a handbag.

ko: 신도들이 봉헌금 대신 비트코인 지갑을 바치기 시작했습니다. 화면 속 숫자가 하루에도 몇 번씩 춤춥니다.
mt: The believers began to offer Bitcoin wallets instead of bags, where the numbers on the screen dance a few times a day.
en: Followers have started offering Bitcoin wallets instead of cash. The numbers on the screen dance several times a day.

ko: 재벌가 장녀가 입교하며 집안의 미술관 열쇠를 내밉니다. 열쇠고리에 다이아몬드가 박혀 있습니다.
mt: The bee opens the door of the eldest girl, opens the key to the art museum in the house, and it's got diamonds stuck in the key ring.
en: The eldest daughter of a chaebol family joins the cult and hands over the keys to the family art museum. The keyring is set with diamonds.

ko: 신전 지하에 개인 보물고를 만들자는 설계도가 올라왔습니다. 두꺼운 강철문 도면이 책상을 덮습니다.
mt: The plans for building private treasure chests in the temple basement are up, and the thick steel doors cover the desk.
en: Blueprints arrive for a private treasury beneath the temple. Drawings of a thick steel door cover the desk.

ko: 요트 회사가 신의 순례를 위한 호화 요트를 헐값에 넘기겠다고 합니다. 갑판에는 샴페인 잔이 늘어서 있습니다.
mt: The yacht company says they're going to hand over the luxury yachts for God's pilgrimage to the streets, and on deck there are plenty of champagne glasses.
en: A yacht company offers to let a luxury yacht go cheap for the god's pilgrimages. Champagne glasses line the deck.

ko: 신도들이 백 가지 요리로 차린 성찬을 준비했습니다. 긴 식탁 끝이 보이지 않습니다.
mt: The faithful have prepared a hundred dishes, and there's no end to the long table.
en: Your followers have prepared a holy banquet of a hundred dishes. The end of the long table is out of sight.

ko: 수십 년 묵은 귀한 술이 봉헌되었습니다. 병을 따자 방 안이 꿀처럼 달콤한 향으로 가득 찹니다.
mt: A few decades of old precious wine has been dedicated. When the bottle is picked, the room is filled with sweet honey.
en: A rare liquor aged for decades has been offered. When the bottle is opened, the room fills with a scent sweet as honey.

ko: 유명 셰프가 신을 위한 비밀 코스를 올리겠다고 합니다. 은빛 뚜껑 아래서 김이 새어 나옵니다.
mt: A famous chef says he's going to post a secret course for God, and under a silver cap comes the steam.
en: A famous chef offers to serve a secret course for the god. Steam escapes from beneath silver cloches.

ko: 금식 기간을 끝내는 잔치를 어떻게 열지 정해야 합니다. 굶주린 신도들의 눈이 당신을 향합니다.
mt: The eyes of the hungry believers are toward you.
en: You must decide how to hold the feast that ends the fast. The eyes of your hungry followers turn to you.

ko: 새벽 시장 상인들이 가장 좋은 물건을 신전에 바치고 싶어 합니다. 생선 비늘이 아침 햇살에 반짝입니다.
mt: The mayors of the morning want to give the best stuff to the godfather, and the fish scales glow in the morning sun.
en: Merchants from the dawn market want to offer their finest goods to the temple. Fish scales glitter in the morning sun.

ko: 신도들이 당신에게 직접 음식을 먹여 드리겠다고 청합니다. 은 숟가락을 든 손들이 줄지어 기다립니다.
mt: The faithful ask you to feed them themselves. The hands with the silver spoon wait in rows.
en: Your followers ask to feed you with their own hands. Hands holding silver spoons wait in line.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 지독한 허기를 호소합니다. 위장이 뒤틀리고 기운이 빠집니다.
mt: The host's body complains of a terrible hunger: it's upset, it's weak.
en: The host's body cries out with a terrible hunger. Your stomach twists and your strength drains away.

ko: 포도 수확철을 맞아 신도들이 포도주 축제를 열자고 합니다. 맨발로 포도를 밟는 통이 마당에 놓였습니다.
mt: At the time of the grape harvest, members of the congregation want to hold a wine festival, and there's a bowl of barefoot grapes in the yard.
en: It is grape harvest season, and your followers want to hold a wine festival. Vats for treading grapes barefoot sit in the courtyard.

ko: 한 신도가 직접 기른 송아지를 제물로 바치겠다고 합니다. 송아지 목에 꽃목걸이가 걸려 있습니다.
mt: A Shintoist says he's going to sacrifice a calf that he's raised with a flower necklace on his neck.
en: A follower offers a calf he raised himself as a sacrifice. A garland of flowers hangs around its neck.

ko: 달콤한 과자를 굽는 신도들이 신전 부엌을 차지했습니다. 버터와 설탕 냄새가 기도실까지 스며듭니다.
mt: The faithful roasting sweet cakes have taken over the temple kitchen, butter and sugar smell all the way to the room.
en: Followers baking sweets have taken over the temple kitchen. The smell of butter and sugar seeps all the way into the prayer room.

ko: 희귀한 송로버섯이 봉헌품으로 들어왔습니다. 작은 상자에서 흙냄새와 사향이 번집니다.
mt: A rare cane mushroom has come into the dedicated form, from a small box of earth odors and musk.
en: Rare truffles have arrived as an offering. The scent of earth and musk spreads from a small box.

ko: 교단 창립 기념일 연회를 준비할 때입니다. 연회장 예약 담당자가 메뉴판을 내밉니다.
mt: It's time to prepare for the school's founding anniversary banquet. The chairman of the conference hall pops up the menu.
en: It is time to prepare the banquet for the cult's founding anniversary. The banquet hall's booking manager hands you a menu.

ko: 신도들 사이에서 신이 먹다 남긴 음식이 병을 낫게 한다는 소문이 돕니다. 당신의 식탁 주변에 사람들이 서성입니다.
mt: There is a rumor among the faithful that God's food that he leaves behind heals the disease.
en: A rumor spreads among followers that the god's leftovers cure illness. People hover around your table.

ko: 술에 취한 신도들이 밤새 당신의 이름을 부르며 노래합니다. 빈 술병이 마당을 굴러다닙니다.
mt: A drunken congregation sings your name all night long. An empty bottle runs through the yard.
en: Drunken followers sing your name all night long. Empty bottles roll across the courtyard.

ko: 금지된 열매라 불리는 이국의 과일이 들어왔습니다. 갈라진 과육에서 붉은 즙이 흘러내립니다.
mt: There's a foreign fruit called the forbidden fruit, which flows from the broken flesh.
en: An exotic fruit called the forbidden fruit has arrived. Red juice runs from its split flesh.

ko: 신도들이 당신을 위한 옥좌를 만들자고 합니다. 목수들이 흑단 원목을 마당에 내려놓았습니다.
mt: The faithful ask me to make a throne for you. The carpenters put the ebony tree down in the yard.
en: Your followers want to build you a throne. Carpenters have laid ebony logs in the courtyard.

ko: 지역 정치인이 선거 지원을 부탁하며 고개를 숙입니다. 그는 당선되면 무엇이든 하겠다고 약속합니다.
mt: A local politician bows to ask for election support, and he promises to do anything when elected.
en: A local politician bows his head and asks for your support in the election. He promises to do anything if he wins.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 생일을 국경일처럼 기념하자고 합니다. 행진용 깃발 시안이 책상 위에 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: The faithful ask you to celebrate your birthday as if it were a border day.
en: Your followers want to celebrate your birthday like a national holiday. Draft designs for parade banners are spread across the desk.

ko: 경쟁 교단의 지도자가 무릎 꿇고 합병을 청하러 왔습니다. 그의 뒤로 신도들이 불안하게 웅성입니다.
mt: The leader of the rival movement has come to kneel down and ask for a merger, and behind him is a nervous and vocalization of the faithful.
en: The leader of a rival cult has come on his knees to ask for a merger. Behind him, his followers murmur uneasily.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 거대한 동상을 산 위에 세우자고 합니다. 조감도 속 동상이 구름을 뚫고 서 있습니다.
mt: The faithful are asking you to build your huge statue on the mountain, and the statue of compassion stands through the clouds.
en: Your followers want to erect a colossal statue of you on the mountain. In the aerial rendering, it pierces the clouds.

ko: 신도들이 당신 앞에서 엎드려 절하는 예법을 정하자고 합니다. 예법서 초안에는 절의 횟수까지 적혀 있습니다.
mt: Let's say that the faithful fall down before you, bowing down, and in the first part of the book, it's written down to the number of verses.
en: Your followers want to set a protocol for prostrating before you. The draft even specifies the number of bows.

ko: 방송국이 교주 인터뷰를 황금 시간대에 내보내겠다고 합니다. 조명 아래 빈 의자가 당신을 기다립니다.
mt: The station says they're going to send you the main interview at a time of gold. Empty chairs under the light wait for you.
en: A TV network offers to air an interview with the cult leader in prime time. An empty chair waits for you under the lights.

ko: 측근 하나가 당신의 권위를 등에 업고 신도들 위에 군림하고 있습니다. 그의 방에서 큰 웃음소리가 들립니다.
mt: One of the aides carries your authority on your back and dominates the faithful, and there's a big laugh in his room.
en: One of your inner circle is lording it over the followers on the strength of your Authority. Loud laughter comes from his room.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 이름을 딴 도시를 세우자는 꿈을 이야기합니다. 지도 위에 붉은 원이 그려져 있습니다.
mt: The believers dream of building a city named after you. There's a red circle on the map.
en: Your followers dream aloud of founding a city named after you. A red circle is drawn on the map.

ko: 근처 마을 이장이 마을 전체를 교단에 바치겠다고 찾아왔습니다. 그의 손에 마을 인감이 들려 있습니다.
mt: A nearby village head came to give the whole village to the school, and he had a village in his hand.
en: The head of a nearby village comes to offer the entire village to the cult. He holds the village seal in his hand.

ko: 신도들이 당신을 신이라 부르는 것만으로는 부족하다며 새 칭호를 지어 올렸습니다. 두루마리에 긴 존호가 적혀 있습니다.
mt: It's not enough for the faithful to call you God, it's a new title, it's a long John on the scroll.
en: Your followers say calling you a god is not enough and present a new title. A long honorific is written on the scroll.

ko: 대기업 회장이 은밀한 후원을 제안하며 자신을 후계 사제로 삼아 달라고 합니다. 그의 시계가 묵직하게 빛납니다.
mt: The president of a large company offers secret sponsorship and asks him to be a secondary priest.
en: The chairman of a conglomerate offers secret backing and asks to be made your successor priest. His watch gleams heavily.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 말씀 한마디 한마디를 법으로 삼자고 합니다. 법전 편찬 위원회가 꾸려졌습니다.
mt: The faithful ask you to make a single word of yours as a law.
en: Your followers want every word you speak to become law. A committee has been formed to compile the code.

ko: 경호원을 거느리자는 제안이 올라왔습니다. 검은 양복의 사내들이 문 앞에 일렬로 섰습니다.
mt: The offer was made to take security guards, and there was a row of men in black suits standing at the door.
en: Someone proposes you keep bodyguards. Men in black suits stand in a row at the door.

ko: 교단의 깃발을 시청 앞 광장에 꽂자는 의견이 나옵니다. 광장 한가운데 깃대가 비어 있습니다.
mt: The idea is to put the flag in the front square, and the flag is empty in the middle of the square.
en: Someone suggests planting the cult's flag in the plaza in front of city hall. The flagpole at its center stands empty.

ko: 정광교 사제가 설교 중에 새로 생긴 교단을 조심하라고 경고했다는 소식이 들립니다. 그의 설교 영상이 조회 수를 올립니다.
mt: We hear that the Ching priests warned us to watch out for the new order in their sermons.
en: Word comes that a priest of the Church of Righteous Light warned his congregation about a new cult. The video of his sermon racks up views.

ko: 만수원이 신전 맞은편에 무료 급식소를 열었습니다. 김이 오르는 국솥 앞에 사람들이 줄을 섭니다.
mt: The Mansoo opened a free kitchen on the other side of the temple, and people lined up in front of Kim's cooking pot.
en: The Garden of Plenty has opened a free soup kitchen across from the temple. People line up before steaming pots of soup.

ko: 기도 중 낯선 정적이 귀를 막습니다. 묵언회의 신이 당신을 엿보고 있는 것 같습니다.
mt: It's like the God of the Silence is looking at you.
en: A strange silence plugs your ears mid-prayer. The god of the Order of Silence seems to be watching you.

ko: 신도 하나가 정광교 전도지를 받아 왔습니다. 전도지에는 거짓 신을 경계하라고 적혀 있습니다.
mt: One of the Shintoists has been given a regular lighted message, and the tract says to be on guard against false gods.
en: A follower comes back with a Church of Righteous Light tract. It warns against false gods.

ko: 적검회 순례단이 붉은 깃발을 들고 신전 앞을 지나갑니다. 그들의 노래가 유난히 크게 울립니다.
mt: A pilgrimage to the Red Cross passes through the temple with a red flag, and their songs are unusually loud.
en: Pilgrims of the Red Sword Society march past the temple bearing red banners. Their singing rings unusually loud.

ko: 오래된 성당의 종이 당신이 기도할 때마다 어긋난 박자로 울립니다. 신도들이 불길하다며 수군거립니다.
mt: The old cathedral bell rings with a broken beat whenever you pray, and the faithful say it's ominous.
en: The bell of an old cathedral tolls off-beat every time you pray. Your followers whisper that it is an ill omen.

ko: 만수원 신도들이 당신의 신도들에게 수확제 초대장을 돌립니다. 초대장 봉투에 곡식 낟알이 들어 있습니다.
mt: The majority of the faithful turn the harvest invitation to your faithful. The invitation envelope has grain in it.
en: Followers of the Garden of Plenty hand out harvest festival invitations to your followers. Each envelope holds a few grains.

ko: 다른 신의 사자라 자처하는 노인이 당신을 찾아와 오래 바라보다 떠났습니다. 문턱에 젖은 발자국이 남아 있습니다.
mt: An old man who claimed to be another lion of God came to you and looked at you for a long time and left with wet footprints on the threshold.
en: An old man claiming to be the messenger of another god came, stared at you a long while, and left. Wet footprints remain on the threshold.

ko: 정광교가 공개 교리 토론을 신청해 왔습니다. 토론장 단상에는 두 개의 의자가 마주 놓여 있습니다.
mt: The Chingyo has come up with a public doctrinal debate, and on the stage of the debate, there are two chairs facing each other.
en: The Church of Righteous Light has challenged you to a public debate on doctrine. Two chairs face each other on the stage.

ko: 당신의 교리가 이단 문헌을 베꼈다는 주장이 신학 잡지에 실렸습니다. 기사에는 대조표까지 붙어 있습니다.
mt: The claim that your doctrine copied the pagan literature was published in a theological magazine, even with a balance sheet in the article.
en: A theology journal claims your Doctrine was copied from heretical texts. The article even includes a comparison chart.

ko: 묵언회 수도사들이 신전 앞에서 침묵 시위를 벌입니다. 그들은 입에 하얀 천을 두르고 꼼짝하지 않습니다.
mt: The silent monks protest in front of the temple with white cloth in their mouths, and they are motionless.
en: Monks of the Order of Silence stage a silent protest in front of the temple. White cloth bound over their mouths, they do not move.

ko: 정광교 신학자가 당신의 계시가 모순투성이라는 책을 냈습니다. 서점 진열대 맨 앞에 놓였습니다.
mt: A Chlorist theologian published a book that said that your revelation was contradictory, and it was at the top of the bookstore.
en: A Church of Righteous Light theologian has published a book calling your revelations riddled with contradictions. It sits at the front of the bookstore display.

ko: 만수원이 당신의 향락을 타락이라 부르며 금욕 강연회를 엽니다. 강연장 앞 현수막이 바람에 펄럭입니다.
mt: The majority of people call your fun "lost" and they hold an ascetic talk, and the screen in front of the room is blowing in the wind.
en: The Garden of Plenty brands your indulgence as depravity and holds a lecture on abstinence. A banner flaps in the wind outside the hall.

ko: 신도들 사이에서 교리의 한 구절을 두고 해석 다툼이 벌어졌습니다. 정광교가 그 틈을 파고들고 있다는 말이 돕니다.
mt: There was a conflict of interpretation between the faithful, and it was said that the cult was digging through the gap.
en: A dispute over the meaning of one line of Doctrine has broken out among your followers. Word is the Church of Righteous Light is prying into the gap.

ko: 적검회 무사승이 당신의 신에게 결투를 청하는 편지를 보내왔습니다. 봉투에 마른 피 같은 얼룩이 있습니다.
mt: The Red Crossman has sent you a letter asking your god to fight, and there's a blood stain in the envelope.
en: A warrior monk of the Red Sword Society has sent a letter challenging your god to a duel. The envelope bears a stain like dried blood.

ko: 정광교가 당신의 교리를 반박하는 문답집을 무료로 뿌리고 있습니다. 신도 가방에서 그 책이 발견되었습니다.
mt: It was discovered in the Shinto bag.
en: The Church of Righteous Light is handing out free Q&A booklets refuting your Doctrine. One turned up in a follower's bag.

ko: 만수원이 당신의 신도들에게 일자리와 쌀을 약속하며 개종을 권합니다. 신도 몇이 짐을 싸고 있습니다.
mt: The Man-su has promised your faithful jobs and rice, and they're asking you to convert.
en: The Garden of Plenty urges your followers to convert, promising jobs and rice. A few of them are packing their bags.

ko: 정광교 전도단이 신도들의 집을 한 곳씩 찾아다니고 있습니다. 현관마다 하얀 전단이 끼워져 있습니다.
mt: The Chlorist Mission is searching for one of the faithful's houses, and there's a white flyer on every porch.
en: Church of Righteous Light missionaries are going door to door to your followers' homes. White flyers are tucked into every doorway.

ko: 오래 함께한 측근이 정광교 세례를 받았다는 소식이 들립니다. 그의 빈 방에 당신이 준 성물이 남아 있습니다.
mt: I've heard news that the old affiliated had been baptized as a refinery, that in his empty room, there's something left of the holy thing you gave him.
en: Word comes that a longtime member of your inner circle has been baptized by the Church of Righteous Light. The relic you gave him is left in his empty room.

ko: 묵언회가 당신의 신도들을 산중 침묵 수련에 초대했습니다. 돌아온 이들은 당신의 이름을 부르지 않습니다.
mt: The Silencers have invited your faithful to the silence in the mountains. The returnees will not call you by your name.
en: The Order of Silence has invited your followers to a silent retreat in the mountains. Those who return no longer speak your name.

ko: 적검회가 신도들의 자녀를 무술 도장으로 끌어들이고 있습니다. 부모 신도들이 불안해합니다.
mt: The Red Cross is bringing the children of the faithful to the martial arts. The parents are nervous.
en: The Red Sword Society is luring your followers' children into its martial arts dojo. The parents are uneasy.

ko: 만수원이 당신의 신전 바로 옆 건물을 사들였습니다. 새 간판에 풍요의 낟알 문양이 걸립니다.
mt: The Man-su bought a building right next to your temple, and a new sign of abundance takes place.
en: The Garden of Plenty has bought the building right next to your temple. A new sign bears its grain-of-plenty emblem.

ko: 정광교가 개종자에게 죄를 씻어 주는 정화 의식을 공짜로 해 준다고 광고합니다. 신도들이 자신의 향락을 돌아보며 흔들립니다.
mt: It's advertised that the Ching Ching is free of ritual cleansing that cleanses converts of their sins, and the believers look at their own pleasures and shake them.
en: The Church of Righteous Light advertises free purification rites to wash away converts' sins. Your followers look back on their indulgences and waver.

ko: 신도 가족들이 기성 종교 성직자를 데리고 와 신도를 데려가려 합니다. 신전 앞에서 고성이 오갑니다.
mt: The Shinto family is bringing in an established religious minister, and they're taking him with them, and they're coming up in front of the temple.
en: Followers' families arrive with clergy from established religions to take them home. Shouting erupts outside the temple.

ko: 정광교 공의회가 당신의 교단을 공식 이단으로 선고했습니다. 선고문이 모든 신문 종교면에 실렸습니다.
mt: The Protestant Council has declared your order to be official board of directors, and the preamble has appeared on every side of the religious press.
en: The Council of the Church of Righteous Light has officially declared your cult heretical. The verdict runs in the religion section of every paper.

ko: 이단 선고 이후 신도들이 길에서 손가락질을 받고 있습니다. 한 신도가 울면서 돌아왔습니다.
mt: After Idan's sentence, the believers are being fingered on the street, and one of them came back crying.
en: Since the heresy verdict, your followers are pointed at in the street. One comes back in tears.

ko: 만수원이 당신의 향락을 증언할 전 신도를 내세워 집회를 엽니다. 연단 위 그는 눈물을 흘리며 고백합니다.
mt: On the platform he confesses with tears.
en: The Garden of Plenty holds a rally featuring a former follower who testifies to your indulgences. On the podium, he weeps as he confesses.

ko: 신학교에서 당신의 교리를 반면교사로 가르치기 시작했습니다. 교재 표지에 당신의 문장이 거꾸로 찍혀 있습니다.
mt: You start teaching your doctrines on the side of the seminary, and your sentences are upside down on the cover of the textbook.
en: Seminaries have begun teaching your Doctrine as a cautionary example. Your emblem is printed upside down on the textbook cover.

ko: 묵언회의 저주가 신도들의 꿈을 차갑게 식히고 있습니다. 신도들이 밤마다 아무 꿈도 꾸지 못한다고 호소합니다.
mt: The silence has cooled the dreams of the faithful, who complain that they can't dream at all night.
en: The Order of Silence's curse is chilling your followers' dreams. They complain that they dream nothing at all, night after night.

ko: 정광교가 당신의 교리서를 모아 광장에서 불태우는 의식을 예고했습니다. 장작더미가 쌓이기 시작합니다.
mt: The Chings have gathered your dogma and announced the ritual of burning in the square, and the pile of wood is starting to pile up.
en: The Church of Righteous Light has announced a ritual to burn your scriptures in the plaza. A pile of firewood begins to grow.

ko: 이단 선고를 받은 다른 작은 교단이 동맹을 청해 옵니다. 그들의 신은 오래전에 잊힌 신입니다.
mt: Another small cult with a pagan sentence calls for allies, whose gods are long forgotten gods.
en: Another small cult declared heretical asks for an alliance. Their god is one forgotten long ago.

ko: 신도들 사이에서 정말 우리가 이단이냐는 질문이 조심스럽게 나오기 시작했습니다. 기도실의 빈자리가 늘어납니다.
mt: The question of whether we're really here, amongst the faithful, began to come out with care, and the empty space in the prayer room increases.
en: Followers have begun cautiously asking whether they really are heretics. Empty seats multiply in the prayer room.

ko: 하늘이 붉게 물들고 다른 신들이 마침내 직접 움직였습니다. 신전 지붕 위로 낯선 새 떼가 맴돕니다.
mt: The sky is red and the other gods have finally moved directly, and there's a flock of strange birds hovering over the temple roof.
en: The sky turns red, and the other gods have finally moved themselves. A flock of strange birds circles above the temple roof.

ko: 적검회 신이 당신의 그릇을 노리고 붉은 칼날의 환영을 보냅니다. 거울 속 당신의 목에 붉은 선이 그어져 있습니다.
mt: The Red Cross gives you a vision of the red blade, a red line on your neck in the mirror.
en: The god of the Red Sword Society covets your vessel and sends visions of a red blade. In the mirror, a red line is drawn across your throat.

ko: 묵언회 신이 당신과 그릇 사이의 끈을 끊으려 합니다. 기도할수록 손끝이 차갑게 식습니다.
mt: The more I pray, the more cold my fingertips are.
en: The god of the Order of Silence is trying to sever the bond between you and your vessel. The more you pray, the colder your fingertips grow.

ko: 만수원 신이 당신 신도들의 곳간을 말려 버렸습니다. 신도들의 밭에서 작물이 하룻밤 사이에 시들었습니다.
mt: The Lord of the Gulf has dried up the storehouses of your faithful, and the crops have grown overnight in the fields of the faithful.
en: The god of the Garden of Plenty has dried up your followers' granaries. Crops in their fields withered overnight.

ko: 정광교 신이 당신의 계시를 거짓말로 뒤바꾸는 환청을 신도들에게 퍼뜨립니다. 신도들이 같은 말을 중얼거립니다.
mt: The Ching Spirit spreads voices to the faithful who turn your message into lies.
en: The god of the Church of Righteous Light spreads voices among your followers that twist your revelations into lies. Your followers mutter the same words.

ko: 네 교단이 연합해 성전을 선포했습니다. 각 교단의 깃발이 도시 사방에서 신전을 향합니다.
mt: Four cults united to declare the temple, each flag facing the temple from all sides of the city.
en: The four faiths have united and declared a holy war. Their banners converge on your temple from every corner of the city.

ko: 다른 신 하나가 몰래 사자를 보내 당신 편에 서겠다고 속삭입니다. 사자의 눈동자가 금빛으로 빛납니다.
mt: Another god whispers to send a lion secretly to stand on your side, and the eyes of the lion glow with gold.
en: Another god secretly sends a messenger whispering that it will take your side. The messenger's eyes glow gold.

ko: 신들의 회합이 당신을 심판대에 세우겠다고 통보해 왔습니다. 꿈속에 거대한 원탁과 빈 의자가 보입니다.
mt: I've been informed that the meeting of the gods will put you in judgment, and I can see in my dream a huge table and an empty chair.
en: The assembly of gods informs you that you will be put on trial. In your dreams you see a vast round table and an empty chair.

ko: 동네 커뮤니티에 당신의 기적은 다 짜고 치는 연극이라는 글이 올라왔습니다. 댓글이 수백 개 달렸습니다.
mt: Your miracles in the community have been described as full-blown theater, hundreds of comments.
en: A post on a local forum claims your miracles are all staged. It has hundreds of comments.

ko: 미용실 아주머니들 사이에서 신전 안에서 밤마다 이상한 소리가 난다는 이야기가 돕니다. 신도 하나가 그 말을 엿듣고 왔습니다.
mt: There's a story among the beauty ladies that says that there's a strange sound every night in the temple.
en: Among the ladies at the hair salon, talk goes around of strange noises from the temple every night. A follower overheard it.

ko: 당신이 치유했다던 신도가 사실 원래부터 아프지 않았다는 소문이 퍼집니다. 그 신도의 얼굴이 하얗게 질렸습니다.
mt: Rumor has it that the Shinto you've cured hasn't been sick in the first place, and that Shinto's face is white.
en: A rumor spreads that the follower you supposedly healed was never sick to begin with. The follower's face has gone white.

ko: 유튜버 하나가 신전 앞에서 몰래카메라를 찍고 있습니다. 그는 모자를 깊게 눌러썼습니다.
mt: One of the tutors is taking a secret camera in front of the temple, and he's pressing his hat deep.
en: A YouTuber is filming with a hidden camera outside the temple. His cap is pulled low.

ko: 옆 건물 세입자가 신전의 향 냄새와 음악 소리로 구청에 민원을 넣겠다고 합니다. 그의 손에 녹음기가 들려 있습니다.
mt: The tenants of the building next door say they're going to put the smell of the temple and the sound of music into the sound of the sound of the voice.
en: A tenant next door threatens to complain to the district office about the temple's incense and music. He holds a recorder.

ko: 당신이 사실은 사기 전과자라는 헛소문이 돕니다. 출처를 알 수 없는 사진 한 장이 함께 돌고 있습니다.
mt: There's a rumor that you're actually a fraud criminal, and there's a picture that you don't know where it comes from.
en: A false rumor goes around that you are a convicted fraudster. A photo of unknown origin circulates with it.

ko: 택시 기사들이 신전 앞을 지날 때마다 혀를 찬다는 이야기가 들립니다. 한 기사가 창문을 내리고 침을 뱉고 갑니다.
mt: Every time taxi driver walks in front of the temple, we hear that he puts his tongue on, and a driver puts out his window and spits on it.
en: You hear that taxi drivers click their tongues whenever they pass the temple. One rolls down his window, spits, and drives off.

ko: 신도의 직장 동료들이 그를 사이비에 빠진 사람이라며 따돌린다고 합니다. 그는 회사를 그만둘까 고민합니다.
mt: He's thinking about quitting the company.
en: A follower's coworkers are shunning him for falling into a pseudo-religion. He is thinking of quitting his job.

ko: 지역 신문이 신흥 교단의 호화 생활을 고발하는 기획 기사를 준비 중이라는 정보가 들어왔습니다. 기자가 신도들에게 연락하고 있습니다.
mt: We've been informed that the local newspaper is preparing a project article to decry the luxury of the new order, and a reporter is contacting the congregation.
en: Word comes that the local paper is preparing an exposé on the lavish lives of new cults. A reporter is contacting your followers.

ko: 시사 프로그램 제작진이 잠입 취재를 시도하다 들켰습니다. 그의 가방에서 소형 카메라가 나왔습니다.
mt: A news program crew came by trying to get in, and a small camera came out of his bag.
en: A current affairs show crew was caught trying to go undercover. A tiny camera was found in the reporter's bag.

ko: 의사 협회가 당신의 치유 기적이 환자들의 치료를 방해한다는 성명을 냈습니다. 성명서가 뉴스 속보로 나갑니다.
mt: The Medical Association has announced that your healing miracle interferes with the treatment of patients.
en: The medical association issues a statement that your healing miracles keep patients from getting treatment. It airs as breaking news.

ko: 연예 매체가 당신의 밤 생활을 다룬 폭로 기사를 예고했습니다. 예고편 사진에 흐릿한 실루엣이 찍혀 있습니다.
mt: The entertainment media gave a preview of your night-long exposé with a blurry slulet on the Yemeni photo.
en: An entertainment outlet teases an exposé on your nightlife. The preview photo shows a blurry silhouette.

ko: 전직 신도가 방송에 나와 당신이 기적을 조작했다고 주장합니다. 그의 목소리는 변조되어 있습니다.
mt: His voice has been altered.
en: A former follower goes on air claiming you faked your miracles. His voice is disguised.

ko: 포털 실시간 검색어에 당신의 교단 이름과 사기라는 단어가 함께 올랐습니다. 신도들의 휴대폰이 쉴 새 없이 울립니다.
mt: In the portal real-time search language, the word for your cult name and fraud comes along, and the cell phones of the faithful keep ringing.
en: Your cult's name and the word fraud trend together on the portal's real-time searches. Your followers' phones ring nonstop.

ko: 한 기자가 당신과의 단독 인터뷰를 요청하며 진실을 밝힐 기회를 주겠다고 합니다. 그의 눈빛이 날카롭습니다.
mt: A journalist asks you for a single interview and offers you an opportunity to reveal the truth, and his eyes are sharp.
en: A reporter requests an exclusive interview, offering you a chance to tell the truth. His gaze is sharp.

ko: 종교 비평가가 당신의 기적을 하나하나 과학으로 해부하는 책을 냈습니다. 베스트셀러 목록에 올랐습니다.
mt: A religious critic published a book that revealed every miracle of yours in science, on the best-selling list.
en: A religion critic has published a book dissecting your miracles one by one with science. It made the bestseller list.

ko: 세무서에서 교단 회계 장부를 제출하라는 통지가 왔습니다. 마감일이 일주일 뒤입니다.
mt: The tax office asked me to submit an account book for the school, which is a week from the deadline.
en: The tax office sends notice to submit the cult's account books. The deadline is a week away.

ko: 구청이 신전 건물의 용도 변경 위반을 조사하겠다고 합니다. 조사관이 줄자를 들고 건물을 둘러봅니다.
mt: The hearing is going to investigate the damage to the temple building's use, and the investigator is going to look around the building with a tape measure.
en: The district office will investigate the temple building for zoning violations. An inspector walks around it with a measuring tape.

ko: 경찰이 신도 가족의 실종 신고를 근거로 신전을 방문했습니다. 정복 경찰 둘이 현관에 서 있습니다.
mt: The police visited the temple on the basis of reports of the disappearance of the Shinto family, two conquering police officers standing on the porch.
en: Police visit the temple over a missing persons report filed by a follower's family. Two uniformed officers stand at the entrance.

ko: 국세청 조사팀이 봉헌금 출처를 캐묻습니다. 금고 앞에 조사관들이 앉아 있습니다.
mt: The IRS investigation team is asking where the chest donation comes from, and they're sitting in front of the vault.
en: A National Tax Service team questions the source of your Offerings. Inspectors sit in front of the vault.

ko: 소방서가 신전의 향과 촛불이 화재 위험이라며 특별 점검을 나왔습니다. 점검표에 빨간 줄이 늘어 갑니다.
mt: The fire department has a special check that says the incense and candles of the temple are in danger of fire, and the red line goes up on the checklist.
en: The fire department conducts a special inspection, calling the temple's incense and candles a fire hazard. Red marks pile up on the checklist.

ko: 검찰이 교단 간부 하나를 횡령 혐의로 소환했습니다. 그는 당신에게 어떻게 해야 하냐고 묻습니다.
mt: He asks you what to do.
en: Prosecutors summon one of the cult's officers on embezzlement charges. He asks you what he should do.

ko: 보건소가 신전 부엌의 위생 점검을 나왔습니다. 향연에 쓰인 식재료가 줄줄이 검사대에 오릅니다.
mt: The health center has taken a sanitary check in the temple kitchen, where the food supplies of the smokestation line up on the table.
en: The health center comes to inspect the temple kitchen. Ingredients from the feasts go onto the testing table one after another.

ko: 시청이 교단 소유 건물 하나에 철거 명령을 검토한다는 공문을 보냈습니다. 공문에는 건물 사진이 첨부되어 있습니다.
mt: City Hall sent a message to a church-owned building to review the demolition order.
en: City hall sends an official letter saying it is considering a demolition order for one of the cult's buildings. A photo of the building is attached.

ko: 경찰이 교단 집회를 사전 신고제로 묶었습니다. 신고 없는 모임은 해산시키겠다고 합니다.
mt: The police have tied up the Church's rally with a prior notice, and they say they're going to disband the group that doesn't report it.
en: Police now require advance notice for cult gatherings. Unreported meetings will be dispersed.

ko: 공개 기적을 금지한다는 행정 명령이 내려왔습니다. 위반하면 교단 시설을 폐쇄하겠다고 합니다.
mt: The order has been issued to ban public miracles, and they say that if they violate, they will shut down the institution.
en: An executive order bans public miracles. Violations will mean the closure of cult facilities.

ko: 신전 앞에 경찰 버스가 상주하기 시작했습니다. 드나드는 신도들의 얼굴이 하나하나 촬영됩니다.
mt: The police bus went to the front of the temple, and he was photographed by the faces of each member of the congregation.
en: A police bus is now stationed outside the temple. Every follower coming and going is photographed.

ko: 교단 행사를 위해 빌린 공연장이 계약을 일방적으로 취소했습니다. 위에서 압력이 내려왔다고 합니다.
mt: The director of the studio has canceled the contract on a one-way basis for the Church's event. The pressure has come down from above.
en: The concert hall rented for a cult event has unilaterally canceled the contract. Pressure came from above, they say.

ko: 은행이 교단 계좌 거래를 정지했습니다. 봉헌금을 받을 길이 막혔습니다.
mt: The bank stopped dealing with the hierarchy account. The way to get the dedication money was blocked.
en: The bank has frozen the cult's accounts. You can no longer receive Offerings.

ko: 시민 단체가 신전 앞에서 교단 퇴출 시위를 벌입니다. 확성기 소리가 기도를 덮습니다.
mt: Citizens group are setting out to protest before the temple, and the sound of the loudspeaker covers the prayer.
en: A civic group protests outside the temple, demanding the cult be expelled. Loudspeakers drown out the prayers.

ko: 교단 간부들의 휴대폰이 통신 조회되고 있다는 제보가 들어왔습니다. 간부들이 서로를 의심합니다.
mt: There's a message that the staff's cell phones are being intercepted, and they're suspicious of each other.
en: A tip comes in that the officers' phone records are being pulled. The officers suspect one another.

ko: 국회의원 하나가 신흥 교단 규제법을 발의하며 당신의 교단을 대표 사례로 들었습니다. 법안 이름에 교단 이름이 거론됩니다.
mt: A member of the Parliament, in discussing the law of the new order, heard your order as a representative case, the name of the school being mentioned in the bill.
en: A lawmaker introduces a bill to regulate new cults, citing yours as the prime example. Your cult's name comes up in the bill's title.

ko: 검찰이 교단 해산 명령 청구를 준비한다는 기사가 1면에 실렸습니다. 신도들의 얼굴에서 핏기가 가십니다.
mt: There's an article on the front page saying that the prosecutors are preparing to issue an order to dispersal, and it's blood on the faces of the faithful.
en: A front-page story says prosecutors are preparing to seek a dissolution order against the cult. The color drains from your followers' faces.

ko: 압수 수색 영장을 든 수사관들이 새벽에 신전 문을 두드립니다. 수십 명의 발소리가 복도를 울립니다.
mt: Officers carrying warrants to seize and search the temple door are knocking at dawn, dozens of footsteps are ringing in the hallways.
en: Investigators with a search warrant pound on the temple doors at dawn. Dozens of footsteps echo down the hall.

ko: 법원이 교단 재산 동결 신청을 심리합니다. 방청석에 기자들이 빽빽하게 앉아 있습니다.
mt: A court hearings the church's property freeze application, and there's a bunch of reporters sitting in the audience.
en: The court hears a motion to freeze the cult's assets. Reporters pack the gallery.

ko: 정부가 교단 시설을 하나씩 강제 폐쇄하기 시작했습니다. 다음은 어느 건물일지 아무도 모릅니다.
mt: The government has begun to force the institution to shut down one by one, and nobody knows which building to do next.
en: The government has begun forcibly closing cult facilities one by one. No one knows which building is next.

ko: 해산을 막기 위한 마지막 탄원서를 모을 수 있습니다. 서명대 앞에 신도들이 모였습니다.
mt: You can collect the final petition to prevent the birth of a woman. The faithful gathered in front of the signet.
en: You can gather one last petition to stop the dissolution. Followers gather at the signing table.

ko: 고위 관료 하나가 은밀히 연락해 거래를 제안합니다. 그는 해산을 막아 줄 수 있다고 말합니다.
mt: A high-ranking official calls in secret and proposes a deal, and he says he can stop the dispersal.
en: A high-ranking official secretly contacts you with a deal. He says he can stop the dissolution.

ko: 언론이 교단의 마지막 날을 생중계하겠다며 진을 치고 있습니다. 신전 앞이 방송 장비로 가득합니다.
mt: The press is setting out to live on the last day of the church, and the front of the temple is full of broadcast equipment.
en: The press has camped out to broadcast the cult's last day live. Broadcasting equipment crowds the front of the temple.

ko: 당신을 체포하라는 영장이 발부되었다는 소문이 돕니다. 측근들이 도피를 권합니다.
mt: Word has been heard that a warrant has been issued to arrest you.
en: Rumor says a warrant has been issued for your arrest. Your inner circle urges you to flee.

ko: 아침에 눈을 뜨자 숙주의 손이 당신의 의지와 상관없이 떨립니다. 몸이 아직 신을 완전히 받아들이지 못했습니다.
mt: When you open your eyes in the morning, your hands tremble regardless of your will, your body still hasn't fully accepted God.
en: You wake in the morning to find the host's hands trembling against your will. The body has not yet fully accepted the god.

ko: 거울 속 숙주의 눈동자가 순간 금빛으로 번쩍입니다. 당신을 본 신도가 비명을 삼킵니다.
mt: The eyes of the host in the mirror flash with gold, and the Shintoist who sees you swallows the screams.
en: In the mirror, the host's eyes flash gold for an instant. A follower who sees you stifles a scream.

ko: 숙주의 영혼이 꿈속에서 당신에게 말을 겁니다. 그는 자신의 몸을 돌려 달라고 애원합니다.
mt: The host's soul will speak to you in a dream, and he begs you to turn his body around.
en: The host's soul speaks to you in a dream. He begs you to give his body back.

ko: 큰 기적을 쓴 뒤 코에서 피가 멈추지 않습니다. 하얀 손수건이 붉게 젖어 갑니다.
mt: It's a big miracle, and it doesn't stop bleeding in its nose, and white handkerchiefs get wet red.
en: After a great miracle, your nose will not stop bleeding. A white handkerchief soaks through with red.

ko: 숙주의 옛 연인이 당신을 알아보고 찾아왔습니다. 그녀는 예전처럼 당신의 이름을 부릅니다.
mt: The old lover of hosting came to recognize you, and she calls you by your name as she used to.
en: The host's former lover recognizes you and comes looking. She calls your name the way she used to.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 인간의 쾌락을 그리워하며 밤마다 뒤척입니다. 피부가 메마르고 입술이 갈라집니다.
mt: The host's body looks back at night, missing the pleasures of human beings, the skin is dry and the lips are split.
en: The host's body yearns for human pleasures and tosses every night. Your skin dries out and your lips crack.

ko: 접신이 깊어지자 숙주의 기억과 당신의 기억이 뒤섞입니다. 어린 시절의 골목이 신의 기억처럼 느껴집니다.
mt: As you get deeper, your host's memory mixes with yours, and your childhood alley feels like God's memory.
en: As Communion deepens, the host's memories blend with yours. An alley from his childhood feels like a god's memory.

ko: 숙주의 어머니가 자식을 돌려 달라며 신전 앞에서 울고 있습니다. 그녀는 낡은 사진을 꼭 쥐고 있습니다.
mt: The host's mother is crying in front of the temple, asking for her child back, and she's holding an old picture.
en: The host's mother weeps outside the temple, begging for her child back. She clutches a worn photograph.

ko: 기적을 쓸 때마다 숙주의 머리카락이 한 움큼씩 하얗게 셉니다. 신도들은 그것을 성스러운 표식이라 부릅니다.
mt: Whenever they do a miracle, their host's hair is white by handful, which the faithful call a sacred marker.
en: Every miracle turns a handful of the host's hair white. Your followers call it a holy mark.

ko: 깊은 밤 숙주의 몸이 저절로 공중에 떠오릅니다. 천장이 손끝에 닿을 듯 가깝습니다.
mt: Deep into the night, the host's body floats into the air, and the ceiling is close to reaching its fingertips.
en: Deep in the night, the host's body rises into the air on its own. The ceiling seems close enough to touch.

ko: 숙주의 몸에서 은은한 향기가 나기 시작했습니다. 스치기만 해도 사람들이 고개를 돌립니다.
mt: The host's body began to smell silvery, and people turned their heads at the touch.
en: A faint fragrance has begun to rise from the host's body. People turn their heads at the slightest brush.

ko: 오랜 기적의 여파로 숙주의 심장이 불규칙하게 뜁니다. 가슴 안쪽에서 북소리 같은 박동이 들립니다.
mt: In the aftermath of a long miracle, the host's heart beats irregularly, and inside the chest there's a drum-like beat.
en: After so many miracles, the host's heart beats irregularly. A pulse like a drum pounds deep in your chest.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 다른 신의 신전 앞을 지날 때마다 타는 듯 아픕니다. 피부에 붉은 반점이 올라옵니다.
mt: The host's body burns as it passes through the presence of another god's temple, and the red spot is on his skin.
en: The host's body burns with pain whenever it passes another god's temple. Red blotches rise on your skin.

ko: 신도 하나가 숙주의 몸을 돌봐 주는 시중꾼이 되겠다고 나섭니다. 그는 따뜻한 수건과 향유를 들고 있습니다.
mt: A Shintoist claims to be an attendant who cares for his host's body, holding warm towels and perfumed oils.
en: A follower volunteers to serve as attendant to the host's body. He holds warm towels and scented oil.

ko: 잠든 사이 숙주의 영혼이 몸을 되찾아 거리를 헤매다 돌아왔습니다. 발바닥이 흙투성이입니다.
mt: In the middle of the night, the host's soul returned to his body and wandered back into the streets, and his feet were covered with dirt.
en: While you slept, the host's soul reclaimed the body, wandered the streets, and came back. The soles of your feet are caked with dirt.

ko: 접신 게이지가 넘칠 듯 차오릅니다. 그릇이 신의 힘을 다 담지 못해 손끝에서 빛이 샙니다.
mt: It's a gypsum of ligaments, and the bowl can't hold the full power of God, and it's shining on its fingertips.
en: The Communion gauge is filling to the brim. The vessel cannot hold all of the god's power, and light leaks from your fingertips.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 노화를 멈춘 것 같다는 말이 돕니다. 오래된 사진보다 지금이 더 젊어 보입니다.
mt: It turns out that the host's body seems to have stopped aging, and it looks younger now than the old picture.
en: People say the host's body seems to have stopped aging. You look younger now than in old photographs.

ko: 숙주의 꿈에 거대한 원형 고리가 나타납니다. 고리 한가운데서 누군가 당신을 부릅니다.
mt: There's a huge circle in the master's dream, and in the middle of it someone calls you.
en: A vast ring appears in the host's dreams. From its center, someone calls to you.

ko: 기적을 행한 손바닥에 낙인 같은 문양이 새겨졌습니다. 문양은 지워지지 않고 밤마다 따끔거립니다.
mt: The miracle hand was marked with a branding sign, and it didn't erase it, and it stings at night.
en: A brand-like mark has appeared on the palm that worked the miracle. It will not fade and stings every night.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 지쳐 기적을 쓰려 해도 아무 일도 일어나지 않습니다. 손끝이 차갑게 식어 있습니다.
mt: If your host's body gets tired of doing miracles, nothing happens, your hands are cold and cold.
en: The host's body is so exhausted that nothing happens when you try to work a miracle. Your fingertips are cold.

ko: 신도들이 숙주의 몸을 씻긴 물을 성수로 쓰자고 합니다. 욕실 문밖에 빈 병들이 늘어서 있습니다.
mt: They say, "Let's use the washed water for holy water. There's plenty of bottles outside the bathroom door."
en: Your followers want to use the water that bathed the host's body as holy water. Empty bottles line up outside the bathroom door.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 인간의 음식 맛을 점점 잊어 갑니다. 무엇을 먹어도 재 맛이 납니다.
mt: The host's body gradually forgets the taste of human food, and whatever it eats, it tastes good.
en: The host's body is slowly forgetting the taste of human food. Everything tastes of ash.

ko: 깊은 접신 중 숙주의 입에서 아무도 모르는 고대어가 흘러나옵니다. 받아 적던 신도의 손이 멈춥니다.
mt: Deep down, the host's mouth comes out with an ancient language that no one knows, and the Shinto hand stops.
en: In deep Communion, an ancient tongue no one knows pours from the host's mouth. The follower taking it down stops writing.

ko: 숙주의 그림자가 당신의 움직임을 한 박자 늦게 따라옵니다. 그림자는 숙주의 영혼처럼 고개를 숙이고 있습니다.
mt: Your host's shadow follows you one second late, and it's down like a host's soul.
en: The host's shadow follows your movements a beat late. It hangs its head like the host's soul.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 쾌락에 너무 익숙해져 이제는 웬만한 향락으로는 회복되지 않습니다. 몸이 더 강한 자극을 원합니다.
mt: The host's body has become so accustomed to pleasure that it's no longer recovered from some kind of pleasure, it wants stronger stimulation.
en: The host's body has grown so used to pleasure that ordinary indulgence no longer restores it. It craves something stronger.

ko: 오래 앓던 신도가 당신의 피 한 방울이면 낫는다고 믿고 찾아왔습니다. 그는 작은 은잔을 내밉니다.
mt: The old believer came in believing that a drop of your blood would heal him, and he's throwing out a little silver glass.
en: A follower long ill comes believing a single drop of your blood will cure him. He holds out a small silver cup.

ko: 숙주의 몸에서 다른 이의 상처를 대신 짊어지는 힘이 깨어났습니다. 신도의 멍이 당신의 팔에 옮겨 옵니다.
mt: The power to bear the wounds of another person in your host's body has been awakened, and the bruises of the faithful have been transferred to your arm.
en: A power to take on others' wounds has awakened in the host's body. A follower's bruise moves onto your arm.

ko: 숙주의 생일이 돌아왔습니다. 숙주의 영혼이 오늘 하루만 인간으로 살게 해 달라고 청합니다.
mt: The host's birthday is back, and the host's soul is asking us to let him live as a human being for one day.
en: The host's birthday has come. The host's soul begs to live as a human for just this one day.

ko: 숙주의 몸이 밤새 뜨겁게 타올라 침대 시트가 그을렸습니다. 신의 힘이 그릇을 넘쳐흐릅니다.
mt: The host's body burned hot all night, and the bed sheets were cut, and the power of God was pouring through the bowl.
en: The host's body burned so hot all night that the bedsheets are scorched. The god's power is overflowing the vessel.

ko: 숙주가 남긴 오래된 일기장이 발견되었습니다. 마지막 장에는 신을 만나고 싶다고 적혀 있습니다.
mt: The host's old diary was discovered, and the last chapter says he wants to meet God.
en: An old diary left by the host has been found. On the last page, he wrote that he wanted to meet a god.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 이름으로 서로를 부르는 애칭을 만들었습니다. 복도마다 그 이름이 다정하게 오갑니다.
mt: The faithful have created a nickname for each other in your name, and it's a friendly one in every hall.
en: Your followers have coined pet names for one another from your name. They pass fondly through every hallway.

ko: 새로 온 신도들이 첫 예배에서 무엇을 보고 싶어 하는지 들려옵니다. 그들은 모두 기적을 기대하고 있습니다.
mt: We hear what the new believers want to see in the first service, and they're all expecting a miracle.
en: You hear what the newcomers hope to see at their first service. Every one of them expects a miracle.

ko: 신도들이 경전의 빈 장에 무엇을 채울지 묻습니다. 하얀 종이 위에 촛농이 떨어집니다.
mt: The faithful ask what they're going to fill in the blanks in the holy book, and the wax falls on the white paper.
en: Your followers ask what should fill the blank pages of the scripture. Candle wax drips onto the white paper.

ko: 측근들이 당신 앞에서 누가 더 높은 자리에 설지 다투고 있습니다. 서로의 옷깃을 쥐고 있습니다.
mt: They're arguing about who's going to be higher in front of you, and they're holding each other's collars.
en: Your inner circle quarrels in front of you over who will stand higher. They grip each other by the collar.

ko: 봉헌금 관리 담당이 금고 열쇠를 누구에게 맡길지 묻습니다. 열쇠 꾸러미가 짤랑거립니다.
mt: The account manager asks who the safe keys will be entrusted to them, and the key packets are bogged down.
en: The keeper of the Offerings asks to whom the vault key should be entrusted. The ring of keys jingles.

ko: 신으로서의 확신이 흔들리는 밤입니다. 인간의 몸 안에서 신은 자신이 무엇인지 잊어 갑니다.
mt: It's a night of confidence as a god, and in the human body, God forgets what he is.
en: It is a night when your certainty as a god wavers. Inside a human body, the god is forgetting what it is.

ko: 접신 의식을 신도들 앞에서 공개하자는 의견이 나옵니다. 제단 앞에 방석이 둥글게 깔렸습니다.
mt: The idea is to publicize the received rituals in front of the faithful, and there's a round cushion in front of the altar.
en: Someone suggests performing the Communion ritual openly before the followers. Cushions are laid in a circle before the altar.

ko: 동네 축제 위원회가 교단에 후원을 요청해 왔습니다. 축제 포스터에 후원사 자리가 비어 있습니다.
mt: The local Festival Committee has requested support from the church, and the sponsorship is empty on the festival poster.
en: The neighborhood festival committee asks the cult for sponsorship. The sponsor slot on the festival poster is empty.

ko: 신도들이 당신에게 직접 이름을 지어 받고 싶다고 줄을 섰습니다. 저마다 손에 하얀 종이를 들고 있습니다.
mt: They're saying they want to be named for you, and they're all holding white paper in their hands.
en: Followers line up to receive names from you personally. Each holds a sheet of white paper.

ko: 유명 인플루언서가 신전을 방문하고 싶다고 연락해 왔습니다. 그의 팔로워는 백만 명이 넘습니다.
mt: The famous Flunist has called for a visit to the temple, and there are over a million followers.
en: A famous influencer asks to visit the temple. They have over a million followers.

ko: 신도 하나가 당신의 말씀을 노래로 만들었습니다. 그의 기타 줄이 낡아 있습니다.
mt: One of the gods has made your words a song. His guitar lines are worn out.
en: A follower has turned your words into a song. His guitar strings are worn.

ko: 새로 세운 조각상 앞에서 신도들이 절을 하지 않고 지나칩니다. 조각상의 눈이 텅 비어 보입니다.
mt: The faithful don't bow down in front of the new statue, and the sculpture's eyes look empty.
en: Followers walk past the newly erected statue without bowing. Its eyes look hollow.

ko: 신전 건물의 유지비 고지서가 한꺼번에 날아왔습니다. 봉헌금 장부의 숫자가 빠듯합니다.
mt: The maintenance books of the temple building flew in all at once, and the collection books are very steep.
en: Maintenance bills for the temple building arrive all at once. The figures in the Offerings ledger are tight.

ko: 신도 하나가 당신은 정말 신이냐고 정면으로 묻습니다. 그의 눈에는 두려움과 기대가 섞여 있습니다.
mt: One of the Shintoists asks in the face if you're really God, and his eyes are a mixture of fear and expectation.
en: A follower asks you point-blank whether you are truly a god. Fear and hope mingle in his eyes.

ko: 신전 지하에서 오래된 제단이 발견되었습니다. 제단의 문양이 당신의 낙인과 똑같습니다.
mt: There's an old altar found in the temple basement. The symbol of the altar is the same as your brand.
en: An ancient altar has been discovered beneath the temple. Its markings are identical to your brand.

ko: 지역 언론이 교단의 자선 활동을 취재하고 싶다고 합니다. 기자가 메모장을 들고 기다립니다.
mt: The local press says they want to cover the charity activities, and a reporter waits for them with a memo.
en: The local press wants to cover the cult's charity work. A reporter waits with a notepad.

ko: 신도들이 당신을 위한 비밀 의식을 준비했다며 눈을 가리고 따라오라고 합니다. 복도 끝에서 음악이 흘러나옵니다.
mt: They say they have a secret ritual for you, and they want you to cover your eyes and follow them, and the music comes out at the end of the hall.
en: Your followers say they have prepared a secret rite for you and ask you to follow them blindfolded. Music drifts from the end of the hall.

ko: 대학 동아리가 교단 체험을 신청했습니다. 젊은 학생들이 호기심 어린 눈으로 신전을 둘러봅니다.
mt: A college club asked for an experience, a young student looking around at the temple with curious eyes.
en: A university club has signed up to experience the cult. Young students look around the temple with curious eyes.

ko: 교리 강론회에서 신도가 쾌락과 신성의 경계가 어디냐고 묻습니다. 강론장이 조용해집니다.
mt: In the synod, the Shintoist asks what is the boundary between pleasure and divinity, and the homily is silenced.
en: At a doctrine lecture, a follower asks where the line lies between pleasure and the divine. The hall falls silent.

ko: 측근들이 당신의 행차 때 꽃잎을 뿌리자고 합니다. 바구니마다 장미 꽃잎이 가득합니다.
mt: Let's spread the petals when your phallics are on your way, and every basket is full of roses.
en: Your inner circle wants to scatter petals when you go out in procession. Every basket is full of rose petals.

ko: 신도들이 봉헌금 액수에 따라 자리를 나누자고 합니다. 앞줄 자리에 금색 방석이 놓였습니다.
mt: A group of believers decided to split the table by the amount, and there was a gold cushion in the front row.
en: Your followers want to assign seats according to the size of their Offerings. Gold cushions are placed in the front row.

ko: 승천의 고리 한가운데가 꿈에 선명하게 보입니다. 아직 닿지 못한 빛이 손짓합니다.
mt: In the middle of the crown of heaven, the dream is clear, and the light that we don't yet reach is waving.
en: The center of the ring of ascension appears vividly in your dream. A light you have yet to reach beckons.

ko: 비가 그치지 않는 계절입니다. 빗소리 속에서 접신의 끈이 가늘게 떨립니다.
mt: It's a season where the rain doesn't stop.
en: It is a season of endless rain. In the sound of the rain, the thread of Communion trembles faintly.

ko: 교단이 운영하는 구호소에 노숙인들이 몰려듭니다. 줄이 골목 끝까지 이어졌습니다.
mt: There's a lot of homeless people on the sidelines run by the cults, and the line's on the edge of the alley.
en: Homeless people flock to the cult's relief shelter. The line stretches to the end of the alley.

ko: 오래된 신도 부부가 당신 앞에서 결혼 서약을 새로 하고 싶다고 합니다. 백발의 두 사람이 손을 꼭 잡고 있습니다.
mt: An old Shinto couple wants to renew their marriage vows in front of you, and two white-headed people are holding hands.
en: An elderly couple of followers wish to renew their wedding vows before you. The two white-haired figures hold hands tightly.

ko: 교단 소식지를 거리에서 나눠 주자는 의견이 나옵니다. 인쇄소에서 갓 나온 소식지가 따뜻합니다.
mt: It's an opinion to share the Church's message on the street, and it's warm from the printing press.
en: Someone suggests handing out the cult newsletter on the street. The newsletters are still warm from the printer.

ko: 신도들이 경전 필사 모임을 열었습니다. 붓끝에서 당신의 말씀이 한 자씩 태어납니다.
mt: The faithful have opened a collection of sacred handwriting, and at the end of the brush, your words are born one by one.
en: Your followers have started a scripture-copying circle. Your words are born one character at a time from the tips of their brushes.

ko: 신전 안에서 당신의 초상화를 어디에 걸지 정해야 합니다. 거대한 금테 액자가 벽에 기대어 있습니다.
mt: You have to decide where to hang your portrait inside the temple, and there's a giant gold frame leaning against the wall.
en: You must decide where in the temple to hang your portrait. A huge gilt frame leans against the wall.

ko: 신도 하나가 집을 팔아 봉헌하겠다고 합니다. 그의 손에 집문서가 들려 있습니다.
mt: A Shintoist says he's going to sell his house and dedicate it, and he's got a house document in his hand.
en: A follower says he will sell his house and offer the proceeds. He holds the deed in his hand.

ko: 신이 되기 전의 기억이 희미하게 떠오릅니다. 아무도 기도하지 않던 오랜 공허의 시간입니다.
mt: It's a long, empty time when no one's ever prayed.
en: Memories from before you became a god surface faintly. A long, empty age when no one prayed.

mt: They'll take the perfumed oil and bring it into the room.
en: Take the oil and let them in

ko: 문이 닫히고 촛불이 꺼집니다. 아침의 그는 신을 만졌다고 속삭입니다.
mt: In the morning he whispers that he touched God.
en: The door closes and the candle goes out. In the morning, he whispers that he touched a god.

ko: 문틈으로 새어 나간 소문이 복도를 맴돕니다.
mt: Rumors that have crept through the door wander through the hall.
en: Rumors slip through the crack in the door and drift down the hallway.

mt: It's sent back with perfumed oil.
en: Take only the oil and send them away

mt: There's only the scent of perfumed oil left in the room.
en: Only the scent of oil lingers in the room.

mt: Blessed be you with perfumed oil on his back.
en: Bless him by anointing his back

ko: 손끝이 지나간 자리마다 그가 떨며 기도를 읊습니다.
mt: Every moment his fingertips pass, he trembles and utters a prayer.
en: Wherever your fingertips pass, he trembles and murmurs a prayer.

ko: 그가 놀라 물러서고 어색한 침묵이 흐릅니다.
mt: He's surprised, he's back, and there's an awkward silence.
en: He flinches back, and an awkward silence falls.

mt: We get into the water together.
en: Get in the water with them

ko: 젖은 몸들이 당신을 둘러싸고 물결마다 찬송이 번집니다.
mt: You are surrounded by wet bodies, and every wave is blessed.
en: Wet bodies surround you, and hymns ripple out with every wave.

ko: 누군가 몰래 찍은 사진이 돌기 시작합니다.
mt: It starts with a picture of someone sneaking around.
en: A secretly taken photo begins to circulate.

mt: Only blessings come from the water.
en: Only bless them from the water's edge

ko: 당신이 물을 뿌릴 때마다 신도들이 눈을 감습니다.
mt: Every time you spray it, the faithful close their eyes.
en: Each time you sprinkle the water, your followers close their eyes.

mt: The faithful are allowed to practice their rituals.
en: Let the followers perform the rite themselves

ko: 당신이 없는 자리에서도 그들은 당신의 이름을 부릅니다.
mt: Even when you're not there, they call you by your name.
en: Even in your absence, they call your name.

mt: There's no centrifuge. It's a fall into consciousness.
en: Without anyone at its center, the rite fizzles out.

mt: We pray alone in the locked room.
en: Pray with her alone in a private room

ko: 기도는 밤늦도록 이어지고 그녀는 다음 날 더 큰 봉헌금을 보내옵니다.
mt: Prayer lasts late at night, and she sends a larger dedication fund the next day.
en: The prayer lasts late into the night, and the next day she sends an even larger offering.

ko: 그녀의 자녀들이 교단에 찾아와 소란을 피웁니다.
mt: Her children come to the school to make a fuss.
en: Her children show up at the cult and make a scene.

mt: I pray to the gods in front of me.
en: Pray in front of other followers

mt: I bless her in front of everyone.
en: You bless her in front of everyone.

mt: All I receive is the gift of the bag.
en: Politely accept only the offering

mt: She turns away with an unfortunate look.
en: She leaves with a wistful look.

mt: I lay my hands on the man's flesh, one by one.
en: Lay your hands on bare skin one by one

ko: 손이 닿을 때마다 탄성이 터지고 대기 줄은 더 길어집니다.
mt: Every time you touch your hand, you're going to explode, and you're going to have longer waiting lines.
en: Gasps burst out at each touch, and the line grows even longer.

ko: 손끝만 떨릴 뿐 아무도 낫지 않습니다.
mt: They just shake their hands and nobody gets better.
en: Your fingertips only tremble; no one is healed.

mt: I'm only touching my forehead for a short time.
en: Touch only their foreheads, briefly

mt: The faithful are thrilled with their brief blessings.
en: Even a brief blessing moves your followers.

mt: I see a disappointed face at the formal touch.
en: You see faces disappointed by the perfunctory touch.

mt: Close the waiting room.
en: Close the waiting room

ko: 조용한 밤이 돌아오지만 서운한 기색이 남습니다.
mt: It's a quiet night that comes back, but it's sad.
en: A quiet night returns, but a trace of hurt remains.

mt: We dance together in the middle of the torch.
en: Dance amid the torches with them

ko: 땀에 젖은 몸들이 북소리에 맞춰 당신을 중심으로 소용돌이칩니다.
mt: You have sweaty, wet bodies swirling around you to the sound of the drums.
en: Sweat-soaked bodies whirl around you to the beat of the drums.

ko: 이웃이 신고해 경찰차가 골목을 돌고 갑니다.
mt: Neighbors report it. Police cars are going around the alley.
en: A neighbor calls the police, and a patrol car circles the alley.

mt: I watch them dance high up.
en: Watch the dance from on high

ko: 신도들이 당신의 시선을 받으려 더 격렬하게 몸을 흔듭니다.
mt: The faithful take your attention, and they shake themselves even more violently.
en: Your followers move ever more wildly to catch your gaze.

mt: The dance quickly cools.
en: The dance quickly cools.

mt: Turned into a quiet moon prayer.
en: Change it to a quiet moon-viewing prayer

mt: The prayer follows the moonlight.
en: A tranquil prayer continues beneath the moonlight.

mt: I choose to go to the most beautiful one.
en: Choose the most beautiful one

ko: 촛불이 꺼지고 아침이 오자 간택받은 이는 신을 보았다고 말합니다.
mt: The candle went out, and when morning came, the man who had been chosen said that he had seen God.
en: The candles go out, and when morning comes, the chosen one says they have seen a god.

ko: 간택받지 못한 이들의 질투가 신전을 무겁게 합니다.
mt: The jealousy of those who are not chosen adds to the temple.
en: The jealousy of those not chosen weighs heavily on the temple.

mt: God bless you all with a kiss.
en: Bless them all with a kiss

ko: 입술이 닿은 이마마다 붉은 열기가 번집니다.
mt: Red heat spreads on every forehead that the lips touch.
en: A red heat spreads across every forehead your lips touch.

mt: The ritual scene leaks out.
en: Scenes from the rite leak outside.

mt: I'm delaying my choice.
en: Put off choosing

mt: Waiting increases their cravings.
en: The wait only deepens their longing.

mt: I spend the night as much as I want.
en: Spend the night as the body desires

ko: 숙주의 몸이 만족스럽게 풀어지고 그릇이 다시 단단해집니다.
mt: The host's body is relaxed and the vessel is hardened again.
en: The host's body loosens in satisfaction, and the vessel grows firm again.

ko: 새벽 골목에서 당신을 알아본 사람이 있습니다.
mt: There's a man who recognized you in the alley of dawn.
en: Someone in the dawn alley recognized you.

mt: Cool the heat with cold water.
en: Cool the heat with cold water

ko: 열기는 가라앉지만 몸 안 어딘가가 비어 있습니다.
mt: The heat subsides, but somewhere inside the body is empty.
en: The heat subsides, but something inside your body feels empty.

mt: It turns the heat into a prayer.
en: Turn that heat into prayer

ko: 뜨거운 숨이 기도가 되어 신과 그릇이 하나로 겹칩니다.
mt: Hot breath becomes a prayer, and a god and a vessel become one.
en: Hot breath becomes prayer, and god and vessel merge into one.

mt: The prayers are scattered and the heat is left.
en: The prayer scatters, and only the heat remains.

mt: It takes everything off and it becomes a model.
en: Strip bare and pose

ko: 완성된 그림 앞에서 관람객들이 무릎을 꿇습니다.
mt: The audience kneels in front of the finished picture.
en: Viewers kneel before the finished painting.

mt: The painting is in the middle of a pornographic debate.
en: The painting is caught up in an obscenity controversy.

mt: I'm going to put a thin cloth around it.
en: Pose draped in thin cloth

ko: 천 너머로 비치는 윤곽이 더 큰 상상을 부릅니다.
mt: The outlines that shine over the sky are a bigger picture.
en: The silhouette showing through the cloth invites even wilder imaginings.

ko: 평범한 초상화로 끝나 아무도 주목하지 않습니다.
mt: It ends with an ordinary portrait that nobody notices.
en: It ends up an ordinary portrait that no one notices.

mt: I'm only making you look.
en: Let him paint only your face

mt: A neat icon takes place in a new war.
en: A dignified icon is hung in the temple.

mt: You'll be blessed in front of the gentleman's house.
en: Bless them at the bridal chamber door

ko: 부부는 신의 숨결이 방 안에 머물렀다고 믿습니다.
mt: The couple believe that God's breath stayed in the room.
en: The couple believe the god's breath lingered in the room.

mt: The words of blessing make the atmosphere awkward.
en: Your words of blessing come out tangled, and the mood turns awkward.

mt: I'm going to go in and I'm going to bless you.
en: Enter the bridal chamber to bless them

ko: 문이 닫힌 뒤의 일은 셋만 압니다. 부부는 평생 당신을 섬기겠다고 맹세합니다.
mt: I know only three things after the door is closed. The couple swear to serve you for the rest of their lives.
en: What happens behind the closed door only the three of you know. The couple swear to serve you for life.

mt: Rumors spread to the couple's friendship.
en: The rumor spreads all the way to the bride's family.

mt: Only the talisman of blessing.
en: Give them only a blessing charm

mt: Couples put amulets under pillows.
en: The couple tuck the charm beneath their pillow.

mt: You're gonna burn your incense and open your prayers.
en: Burn thick incense and hold the meeting

ko: 몽롱한 연기 속에서 기도는 신음 섞인 탄식으로 바뀝니다.
mt: In the smoke, prayer is replaced by groaning and groaning.
en: In the hazy smoke, prayers turn into sighs mixed with moans.

ko: 연기에 취해 쓰러진 신도가 병원에 실려 갑니다.
mt: There's a guy in the hospital who's been smoking and fallen.
en: A follower overcome by the smoke collapses and is taken to the hospital.

mt: Lightly scented.
en: Burn the incense lightly

ko: 은은한 향 속에서 신도들이 서로의 손을 맞잡습니다.
mt: In a silvery odor, the believers meet each other's hands.
en: In the faint fragrance, followers clasp each other's hands.

ko: 향이 너무 옅어 아무도 취하지 않습니다.
mt: It's so light that nobody gets drunk.
en: The incense is too faint to intoxicate anyone.

mt: Let him pray with a clear mind.
en: Have them pray with clear minds

ko: 담백한 기도가 끝나고 모두 조용히 돌아갑니다.
mt: After a slouch of prayer, they all go back quietly.
en: After a plain prayer, everyone quietly goes home.

mt: Every year, he sends back a reply from his own pen.
en: Send a handwritten reply to every letter

ko: 답장을 받은 신도들이 밤새 편지를 끌어안고 잠듭니다.
mt: The faithful who receive a reply hold the letter overnight and lock it.
en: Followers who receive replies fall asleep clutching them all night.

mt: A reply is posted on the Internet.
en: One of the replies gets posted online.

mt: I read the hottest letter in my sermon.
en: Read the most passionate letter in your sermon

mt: The ashamed believers cheer up.
en: Embarrassed at first, your followers soon cheer.

mt: The owner of the letter leaves the church with shame.
en: The letter's author leaves the cult in shame.

mt: The letters are burned and burned with incense.
en: Burn the letters as incense

ko: 타오르는 사랑의 말들이 연기가 되어 오릅니다.
mt: The fiery words of love are made to smoke.
en: Burning words of love rise as smoke.

mt: I see her dancing.
en: Stand face to face with her as she dances

ko: 방울 소리가 빨라질수록 두 몸의 거리가 사라집니다.
mt: The faster the bubble sounds, the farther away the two bodies are.
en: The faster the bells ring, the more the distance between your bodies vanishes.

mt: There's too much dancing going on.
en: Whispers go around that the dance went too far.

mt: You're dancing on the altar.
en: Receive the dance atop the altar

ko: 제단 아래 신도들이 숨을 죽이고 그녀의 몸짓을 바라봅니다.
mt: The believers under the altar take their breath and look at her body language.
en: Below the altar, followers hold their breath and watch her every move.

mt: The bubble string is cut off, and the dance stops.
en: The string of bells snaps, and the dance stops.

mt: I respectfully refuse to dance.
en: Politely decline the dance

mt: She collects drops with a sad face.
en: Disappointed, she gathers up her bells.

mt: I admit I met them in a dream.
