mt: The bell is still ringing in the opposite direction.
en: The bell still rings out of time.

mt: I interpret evil as a blessing.
en: Interpret the ill omen as a blessing

ko: 어긋난 종소리가 새 시대의 박자라는 말이 퍼집니다.
mt: There's a strange bell, and there's a new era of gourds.
en: Word spreads that the off-beat bell is the rhythm of a new age.

mt: Interpretation doesn't make sense.
en: The interpretation fails to persuade.

mt: We're moving the time of prayer.
en: Move your prayer time

mt: We pray at dawn to avoid the sound of the bell.
en: You pray at dawn to avoid the bell.

ko: 우리 쪽 수확제를 더 화려하게 연다
mt: We're gonna make our own harvests more colorful.
en: Hold an even grander harvest festival of your own

ko: 신도들은 초대장을 버리고 당신의 잔칫상에 앉습니다.
mt: The faithful abandon the invitation and sit down on your couch.
en: Your followers throw away the invitations and sit at your table.

mt: Some go to both parties.
en: Some attend both feasts.

mt: I'm not going to stop you from responding to your invitation.
en: Do not stop followers who accept the invitation

ko: 관대함은 칭찬받지만 돌아오지 않는 이도 있습니다.
mt: And while generosity is praised, there are those who don't come back.
en: Your generosity is praised, but some never return.

mt: I'm taking out the invitation.
en: Collect the invitations

mt: The faithful send out the invitations without saying a word.
en: Your followers hand them over without a word.

mt: It's called "pressive."
en: Complaints arise that you are being heavy-handed.

mt: I'm after the old man. I'm asking who he is.
en: Chase the old man and ask who he is

ko: 노인은 웃으며 다른 신들이 당신을 지켜본다고 일러 줍니다.
mt: The old man laughs and tells me that other gods watch you.
en: The old man smiles and tells you the other gods are watching you.

ko: 모퉁이를 돌자 노인은 사라지고 서늘함만 남습니다.
mt: When you go around the corner, the old man disappears and you have a coolness.
en: You turn the corner and he is gone, leaving only a chill.

mt: Clear the threshold.
en: Purify the threshold

ko: 향을 피우자 젖은 발자국이 말라 갑니다.
mt: And as she burns the incense, the wet footprints dry up.
en: As the incense burns, the wet footprints dry away.

mt: The footprints won't be erased.
en: The footprints will not fade.

mt: I don't think I've seen it.
en: Pretend you did not see

mt: It's been a couple of days.
en: An uneasy feeling lingers for days.

mt: We're on the stage. We're discussing it head-on.
en: Take the stage and debate head-on

ko: 당신의 말이 끝나자 객석이 일어나 박수를 칩니다.
mt: When your words are over, the audience stands up and claps.
en: When you finish speaking, the audience rises to applaud.

mt: It's a contradiction, and it's stuck.
en: Your contradictions are exposed and you are left speechless.

mt: It's a little miracle in the middle of a debate.
en: Show a small miracle mid-debate

ko: 촛불이 저절로 타오르자 상대가 말을 잃습니다.
mt: The candle is burning on its own, and the opponent loses his horse.
en: A candle bursts into flame on its own, and your opponent falls silent.

mt: It's a trick. It's a trick.
en: Your opponent presses you, calling it a trick.

mt: I refuse to discuss it.
en: Decline the debate

mt: I can't believe he ran away.
en: Word spreads that you ran away.

mt: They're arguing it's ahead of the circle.
en: Counter that your revelation predates the originals

ko: 베낀 것이 아니라 그들이 훔쳐 간 것이라는 말이 설득력을 얻습니다.
mt: It's not something they've stolen, it's something they've stolen.
en: The claim that they stole from you, not the other way around, gains traction.

mt: It's considered to be a bit of a refutation.
en: Your rebuttal is judged feeble.

mt: I'm suing the magazine.
en: Sue the magazine

mt: There's a regular coverage.
en: A correction is printed.

mt: There's more lawsuits, more articles.
en: The lawsuit drags on and the article spreads even further.

mt: All the gods are said to be one.
en: Brush it off, saying all gods are one

ko: 넉넉한 태도에 일부 신도가 고개를 끄덕입니다.
mt: There are some Shintos who nod at all in a generous manner.
en: Some followers nod at your magnanimity.

mt: It's said that the originality of doctrine is broken.
en: Word spreads that your Doctrine's originality has collapsed.

mt: I'm sending the monks a banquet of food.
en: Send banquet food to the monks

ko: 하얀 천을 내린 수도사 하나가 처음으로 웃습니다.
mt: One of the monks who dropped the white cloth laughed for the first time.
en: One monk lowers his white cloth and smiles for the first time.

mt: The monks turn away from food.
en: The monks ignore the food.

mt: Let the faithful face the song.
en: Have your followers answer with song

ko: 노랫소리가 침묵을 밀어내고 신전이 다시 숨 쉽니다.
mt: The song repels the silence and the temple breathes again.
en: The singing pushes back the silence, and the temple breathes again.

mt: There's a noise call.
en: A noise complaint comes in.

mt: I'll leave it as it is.
en: Leave them be

mt: There's a heavy silence that goes to the temple.
en: A heavy silence seeps into the temple.

mt: I write a refutation.
en: Write and publish a rebuttal

ko: 반박서가 그 책 옆에 나란히 놓입니다.
mt: The refutation is next to the book.
en: The rebuttal sits side by side with his book.

mt: There's no refutation.
en: The rebuttal does not sell.

mt: They preach that contradiction is a mystery.
en: Preach that contradiction is the true mystery

mt: Believers accept contradiction as the depth of God.
en: Your followers embrace the contradictions as the god's depth.

mt: It's called the trajectory.
en: People call it sophistry.

ko: 신도들이 그 책을 읽지 못하게 한다
mt: It prevents the faithful from reading it.
en: Forbid your followers from reading the book

ko: 금서가 된 책은 오히려 신비를 잃습니다.
mt: A book that has become a taboo loses its mystery.
en: The banned book, oddly, loses its mystique.

mt: The more you forbid it, the more you learn to read in secret.
en: The more you forbid it, the more followers read it in secret.

mt: Let's have a show in front of the room.
en: Hold a feast outside the lecture hall

ko: 금욕 강연을 듣던 사람들이 하나둘 향연의 냄새를 따라 나옵니다.
mt: People who were listening to the ascetic talk, one by one, followed the smell of the feast.
en: One by one, people at the abstinence lecture follow the scent of the feast outside.

mt: Police are on the move with the charge of theft.
en: Police arrive amid accusations of provocation.

mt: Pleasure is the message of grace.
en: Counter with a sermon that pleasure is grace

ko: 신도들은 죄책감 없이 웃을 수 있게 되었다며 기뻐합니다.
mt: The faithful are happy to be able to laugh without guilt.
en: Your followers rejoice that they can now laugh without guilt.

mt: It sounds like an excuse.
en: The sermon sounds like an excuse.

mt: You'll have to relax for a while.
en: Hold back on indulgence for a while

mt: I can feel it dry.
en: You feel the vessel drying out.

mt: You can't interpret it yourself.
en: Settle the interpretation yourself

mt: Arguments stop in the face of divine interpretation.
en: Before the god's interpretation, the dispute ends.

mt: The defeated side of the congregation is sorry.
en: Followers on the losing side are hurt.

mt: Both interpretations are correct.
en: Declare both interpretations correct

mt: Both sides embrace each other.
en: The two sides embrace.

mt: The doctrine is clouded, and the Chings laugh at it.
en: The Church of Righteous Light sneers that your Doctrine has gone muddy.

mt: I let you fight.
en: Let the dispute run its course

mt: A battle-wepted group of believers is leaving for the sunbaskets.
en: Followers worn out by the quarrel leave for the Church of Righteous Light.

mt: We accept the duel and face it as a miracle.
en: Accept the duel and answer with a miracle

mt: The warrior sword melts in front of you.
en: The warrior monk's sword melts before you.

ko: 검이 그릇의 어깨를 스치고 피가 흐릅니다.
mt: The sword goes through the bowl's shoulder and it bleeds.
en: The blade grazes the vessel's shoulder, and blood flows.

mt: I'm going to send in my proxy.
en: Send a champion in your place

ko: 신도 대표가 버텨 내자 무사승이 물러납니다.
mt: As soon as the Shinto representative gets through, the Moussar retreats.
en: Your followers' representative holds firm, and the warrior monk withdraws.

mt: The agents fall down and the faithful tremble.
en: Your champion falls, and your followers are shaken.

mt: Ignore the letter.
en: Ignore the letter

mt: There's a rumor that it's a coward's God.
en: Rumors spread of a coward god.

mt: I'm going to give you a comment to answer your questions.
en: Publish a commentary answering the Q&A booklet

ko: 해설서를 읽은 신도들이 오히려 신앙을 다집니다.
mt: The believers who read the commentary actually improve their faith.
en: Followers who read the commentary grow firmer in their faith.

mt: I get the opinion that it's too difficult.
en: The commentary is judged too difficult.

mt: He scolds a man who's searched through his bag.
en: Scold the follower whose bag it was found in

mt: The believers are alert.
en: Your followers grow more vigilant.

mt: The doubted believer is hurt and gone.
en: The suspected follower is hurt and leaves.

mt: Read a book and come back and ask questions.
en: Tell them to read the book and come back with questions

mt: The more you answer the question, the harder the doctrine becomes.
en: The more questions you answer, the firmer your Doctrine grows.

mt: The question is raised that doesn't answer.
en: Unanswered questions pile up.

mt: I promise you more rice and work.
en: Promise more rice and jobs

ko: 짐을 싸던 신도들이 다시 짐을 풉니다.
mt: The pack is packed again by the packers.
en: Followers who were packing unpack their bags.

mt: We don't have enough money to keep our word.
en: You lack the money to keep your promise.

mt: For those who want to leave.
en: Hold a feast for those about to leave

ko: 마지막이라던 향연에서 그들은 떠나지 않겠다고 맹세합니다.
mt: They swear they're not going to leave the last one.
en: At what was meant to be a farewell feast, they swear never to leave.

mt: And when it's over, they leave.
en: When the feast ends, they leave.

mt: The one who's leaving is telling him to leave.
en: Tell those who would go to go

mt: The rest of the congregation's eyes became stronger.
en: The eyes of those who remain grow harder.

mt: God puts the charm of blessing on every house.
en: Post blessing charms on every follower's home

ko: 부적이 붙은 문 앞에서 전도단이 발길을 돌립니다.
mt: In front of the left-hand door, the conductors turn their steps.
en: Missionaries turn back at doors bearing charms.

mt: The evangelists take off the charm.
en: The missionaries tear down the charms.

mt: I invite the pulpit to the temple.
en: Invite the missionaries to the temple

ko: 향연에 취한 전도단원 몇이 돌아가지 않습니다.
mt: Several of the evangelists who are on the run don't go back.
en: A few missionaries, intoxicated by the feast, never go back.

mt: The evangelists are shooting inside the temple.
en: The missionaries film the inside of the temple and leave.

ko: 신도들에게 문을 열어 주지 말라고 한다
mt: They tell the faithful not to open the door.
en: Tell your followers not to open their doors

ko: 굳게 닫힌 문 너머로 전단이 쌓입니다.
mt: The altar builds over the tightly closed door.
en: Flyers pile up behind the tightly shut doors.

ko: 그를 찾아가 마지막 밤을 함께 보낸다
mt: Find him and spend the last night together.
en: Go to him and spend one last night together

ko: 새벽에 그는 세례 증서를 찢고 당신의 발치에 엎드립니다.
mt: At dawn he rips the baptismal certificate and falls at your feet.
en: At dawn, he tears up his baptismal certificate and prostrates himself at your feet.

ko: 그는 당신을 밀어내고 정광교에 모든 것을 털어놓습니다.
mt: He's pushing you away, he's throwing everything out in the sunbasket.
en: He pushes you away and tells the Church of Righteous Light everything.

mt: I publicly curse his betrayal.
en: Publicly curse his betrayal

mt: The faithful see the price of betrayal.
en: Your followers see plainly the price of betrayal.

mt: It's cruel, and the faithful are terrified.
en: Your followers are terrified, calling it cruel.

mt: God bless his choice.
en: Bless his choice

mt: There's plenty of God left.
en: You are remembered as a generous god.

mt: To awaken the silence of those who have returned to enjoy themselves.
en: Break the returnees' silence with indulgence

ko: 뜨거운 밤이 지나자 그들의 입에서 다시 당신의 이름이 흘러나옵니다.
mt: After the hot night, your name comes out of their mouths again.
en: After a heated night, your name flows from their lips once more.

mt: They're not talking to each other.
en: They never open their mouths.

mt: They receive it and regain their dreams.
en: Reclaim their dreams through Communion

ko: 당신의 목소리가 그들의 꿈속 침묵을 깨뜨립니다.
mt: Your voice breaks their dream silence.
en: Your voice shatters the silence in their dreams.

mt: A cold silence takes over a miracle.
en: The cold silence swallows the miracle.

mt: I forbid you to participate in the training.
en: Forbid attending the retreat

mt: Some of the people who have spoken against the ban are gone.
en: A few who resent the ban leave for good.

ko: 신전에서 더 즐거운 청년 모임을 연다
mt: We have a more pleasant youth gathering at the temple.
en: Hold a more fun youth gathering at the temple

ko: 청년들이 도장 대신 신전 마당에 모입니다.
mt: Young men gather in temple courtyards instead of chops.
en: The young people gather in the temple courtyard instead of the dojo.

mt: Young people quickly get bored.
en: The young people quickly grow bored.

mt: Gather the parents together and reassure them of their blessings.
en: Gather the parents and reassure them with a blessing

mt: The relief comes back to the parents' faces.
en: Relief returns to the parents' faces.

mt: Anxiety doesn't subside easily.
en: The anxiety does not easily subside.

mt: Miracle threats in front of the chops.
en: Threaten the dojo with a miracle

mt: The stamp sign breaks in the middle of the night.
en: The dojo's sign splits in the middle of the night.

mt: The police are investigating the damage.
en: Police investigate the property damage.

mt: A tower higher than the next building.
en: Raise a tower taller than the building next door

ko: 당신의 탑 그림자가 낟알 간판을 덮습니다.
mt: Your tower shadow covers the kernels.
en: Your tower's shadow falls over the grain sign.

mt: We have a building permit issue.
en: A building permit problem arises.

mt: We invite the members of our neighborhood to the feast.
en: Invite the neighbor's followers to a feast

ko: 낟알 간판 아래 사람들이 당신의 향연 소식을 속삭입니다.
mt: Under the kernels, people whisper the news of your smoke.
en: Beneath the grain sign, people whisper news of your feast.

mt: The invitation is ignored.
en: The invitation is ignored.

ko: 이웃의 쌀자루를 따라 신도 몇이 넘어갑니다.
mt: A few shoes follow the neighbor's rice sack.
en: A few followers drift over, following the neighbor's sacks of rice.

mt: I declare that there is no sin in pleasure.
en: Declare that there is no sin in indulgence

ko: 죄책감을 벗은 신도들이 오히려 더 깊이 당신을 섬깁니다.
mt: The guilty believers serve you more deeply.
en: Freed of guilt, your followers serve you all the more deeply.

mt: The insecure believers are still shaken.
en: Anxious followers still waver.

mt: It creates our own cleansing ritual.
en: Create a purification rite of your own

ko: 우유와 꿀로 씻는 의식이 신도들을 다시 묶습니다.
mt: The ritual of washing with milk and honey is binding the faithful back together.
en: A rite of washing in milk and honey binds your followers once more.

mt: You can see consciousness.
en: The rite looks clumsy.

mt: I leave you with a shaking cult.
en: Leave the wavering followers be

mt: Some of them are headed for the Chlorist Baptism.
en: A few head for the Church of Righteous Light's baptismal font.

mt: The gods make their own choices.
en: Let the follower choose

ko: 신도가 가족 앞에서 당신을 택하겠다고 말합니다.
mt: The Shintoist says he'll choose you in front of his family.
en: The follower tells their family they choose you.

mt: The congregation follows the family in tears.
en: The follower leaves in tears with their family.

mt: The priest and his family will be at the feast.
en: Seat the clergy and family at a feast

ko: 술잔이 돌자 가족마저 당신의 축복을 청합니다.
mt: As soon as the drink is over, even your family will ask for your blessing.
en: As the wine goes around, even the family asks for your blessing.

mt: They're brainwashing, and they're sending their family to the press.
en: The family tips off the press, calling it brainwashing.

mt: I'm gonna lock the door.
en: Lock the doors

mt: The faithful remain, but there is suspicion of imprisonment.
en: The follower stays, but suspicions of confinement arise.

mt: Police are on their way.
en: The police are called in.

mt: I pronounce the sentence a medal of glory.
en: Proclaim the verdict a badge of honor

mt: The story of God being persecuted burns the faithful.
en: The story of a persecuted god sets your followers ablaze.

mt: Fearful believers are shaken.
en: Frightened followers waver.

mt: I answer to the Council with a great miracle.
en: Answer the Council with a great miracle

mt: Newspapers with preambles burn down at one hour a day.
en: Every newspaper carrying the verdict bursts into flame at the same moment.

mt: Miracles fail, leaving us only with ridicule.
en: The miracle fails, leaving only ridicule.

mt: Quietly lower yourself.
en: Quietly lie low

mt: For a while, the eyes of the other gods soften.
en: For a while, the other gods' gaze softens.

mt: I carry my fingertips in my arms, and I comfort them.
en: Embrace and comfort the follower who was mocked

ko: 당신의 품에서 신도의 울음이 웃음으로 바뀝니다.
mt: In your arms, the cries of believers turn into laughter.
en: In your arms, the follower's tears turn to laughter.

mt: The wound doesn't heal easily.
en: The wound does not heal easily.

mt: We give the believers the golden tokens.
en: Hand out golden insignia to your followers

ko: 황금 표식을 단 신도들이 고개를 들고 거리를 걷습니다.
mt: The golden marker stands on the street with its head up.
en: Wearing the golden insignia, your followers walk the streets with heads held high.

mt: The marker becomes a target.
en: The insignia become targets.

mt: They're telling me to stay away from my house.
en: Tell them to stay indoors

mt: The congregation's world narrows into the temple.
en: Your followers' world shrinks to within the temple walls.

mt: I'll bring back my former congregation.
en: Bring the former follower back into the fold

ko: 그는 다음 집회에서 모든 증언을 번복합니다.
mt: He repeats all testimony at the next rally.
en: At the next rally, he retracts all his testimony.

mt: They're even exposed to return attempts.
en: Even your attempt to win him over is exposed.

mt: Enjoyment was blessed to be held.
en: Hold a counter-rally declaring indulgence a blessing

ko: 맞불 집회의 신도들이 행복한 얼굴로 간증합니다.
mt: It's a happy face with the right members of the rally.
en: Followers at the counter-rally testify with happy faces.

mt: Meetings are clashing.
en: The rallies escalate into a clash.

mt: I'm silent.
en: Stay silent

mt: Only the testimony remains.
en: Only the testimony remains, and it spreads.

mt: I'm secretly inviting new students.
en: Secretly invite the seminarians

ko: 반면교사를 배우던 신학생 몇이 당신의 진짜 얼굴에 매혹됩니다.
mt: On the other hand, some of the seminarians who were learning teachers are fascinated by your real face.
en: A few seminarians who studied you as a cautionary tale are captivated by your true face.

mt: The invitation is announced to the seminary.
en: Word of the invitation reaches the seminary.

ko: 거꾸로 찍힌 문장을 새 상징으로 삼는다
mt: Put backwards sentences as new symbols.
en: Adopt the upside-down emblem as a new symbol

mt: The inverted sentence becomes a symbol of resistance.
en: The inverted emblem becomes a symbol of resistance.

mt: Meaning doesn't get through very well.
en: The meaning does not come across well.

mt: The doctrine is less popular.
en: Your Doctrine's reputation erodes little by little.

ko: 신도들과 한 방에서 잠들어 꿈을 나눈다
mt: I sleep in one room with the faithful, and I share my dreams with them.
en: Sleep in one room with your followers and share their dreams

ko: 살을 맞댄 채 잠든 신도들의 꿈에 다시 온기가 돕니다.
mt: I'm back in the dream of the sleeping believers.
en: Warmth returns to the dreams of followers sleeping skin to skin.

mt: Dreams don't come back, rumors do.
en: The dreams do not return, only rumors.

mt: I kick the curse with a strong reception.
en: Lift the curse through powerful Communion

ko: 차가운 장막이 찢어지고 신도들이 다시 꿈을 꿉니다.
mt: Cold tents are torn apart, and the faithful are dreaming again.
en: The cold veil tears, and your followers dream again.

mt: A reaction of the curse hits the vessel.
en: The curse's backlash strikes the vessel.

mt: We change the prayer before we go to sleep.
en: Change the bedtime prayer

mt: The new prayer works a little bit.
en: The new prayer has some effect.

mt: There's no change.
en: Nothing changes.

ko: 불길 속에서도 타지 않는 기적을 보인다
mt: It's a miracle that doesn't even burn in the fire.
en: Show the miracle of not burning amid the flames

ko: 불길 속에서 교리서 한 권이 멀쩡히 떠오릅니다.
mt: In the flames, I think of a single volume of dogma.
en: Amid the flames, a single book of scripture rises unscathed.

mt: All the books become ashes.
en: Every book turns to ash.

mt: On the same day, we'll have a book reading.
en: Hold a scripture reading on the same day

ko: 불타는 광장과 달리 신전에는 말씀이 울려 퍼집니다.
mt: Unlike the burning square, the temple is filled with words.
en: Unlike the burning plaza, the temple resounds with the word.

mt: Less attendance at the reading session.
en: Few people show up to the reading.

mt: I'm gonna re-print the book, and I'm gonna spread it for free.
en: Reprint the book and hand it out free

ko: 불태운 만큼 더 많은 책이 거리로 나갑니다.
mt: More books go into the streets as much as they burn.
en: For every book they burn, more hit the streets.

mt: The printery refuses to trade.
en: The print shop refuses to do business with you.

mt: I'm absorbing the forgotten cult of God.
en: Absorb the cult of a forgotten god

ko: 잊힌 신의 마지막 신도들이 당신에게 오래된 비밀을 바칩니다.
mt: The last believers of the forgotten God give you an old secret.
en: The forgotten god's last followers offer you an ancient secret.

mt: There's a lot of blame for the fact that the cults have come together.
en: Accusations that the heretics have banded together grow louder.

mt: We make an ally.
en: Form an alliance as equals

mt: There's a solidarity between those who are persecuted together.
en: Those persecuted together find solidarity.

mt: An alliance becomes a target.
en: The alliance only makes you a bigger target.

mt: I refuse.
en: Refuse

mt: They avoid the gaze of other gods.
en: You stay out of the other gods' sight.
